hypothesis: The DFlash2 mismatch is caused by the target Q4_K_M batch-8 verification path using a different kernel or floating-point accumulation order than autoregressive batch-1 decode, not by an unverified draft token. If true, the target-only and DFlash2 top candidates at the divergence will be close and stable within each path, making an exact n=8 Q4_K kernel a correctness requirement as well as a speed target.

protocol.prompt: Explain in four sentences why CPU language-model decode is memory-bandwidth bound.

required_receipts: raw responses with token IDs and top-five pre-sampling probabilities
first mismatch index and both top-five candidate sets
decision_rule: Classify the mismatch as target batch-path numerical divergence only if DFlash2's mismatching token is the top target-verification candidate returned by the runtime, not an accepted draft outside the target top candidate. Otherwise classify it as a speculative verification implementation defect.
stop_rule: Run exactly one target-only and one DFlash2 completion and do not tune width, quantization, or kernels in this diagnostic.
claim_boundary: One-prompt mismatch diagnosis only; no performance, quality, losslessness, or final-node claim.
